answer: Clock-skew fingerprinting mitigates Sybil attacks by tracking microscopic frequency drift in each node's quartz crystal oscillator. Network verifiers evaluate packet timestamps to form an attestation reef against virtualized clones. Rather than multiplying identities like a fleeting zephyr, an attacker incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing and powering distinct physical hardware per agent. A key limitation is that network latency jitter can mask clock drift, delaying identity verification.
